- bed_double: height 0.5 m, size options [1.4, 2.0], [1.6, 2.0], [1.8, 2.0] (usually against a wall)

- nightstand: height 0.5 m, size options [0.4, 0.4], [0.5, 0.4], [0.6, 0.45]

- bookshelf: height 1.8 m, size options [0.8, 0.3], [1.0, 0.35], [1.2, 0.4] (usually against a wall)

Rules that are checked afterwards (pieces that fail are moved or removed):
- every footprint lies fully inside the room polygon; pieces do not overlap;
- keep 0.6 m free in front of beds, sofas, desks and wardrobes (front = the -Y side at rotation 0, rotated with the piece);
- keep a 0.9 m wide walkway from every door to every other door and window;
- keep the door swing free: a half circle with the door width as radius inside the room the door opens into, and 0.6 m in front of every door;
- within 0.3 m of a window nothing may be taller than the sill; beds, sofas and tables may stand under a window;
- a piece with against_wall true must touch a wall with its back edge (its +Y side at rotation 0): choose rotation_deg so the back faces the wall (0 = back to a wall on the +Y side, 90 = back to a wall on the -X side, 180 = back to a wall on the -Y side, 270 = back to a wall on the +X side) and set the centre half the depth away from the wall.

A good layout for this room type: one bed (bed_double for a master bedroom, bed_single for a children's room) with the headboard against a wall and not under the door, a nightstand on each free side of a double bed, one wardrobe against a wall, optionally a desk with a chair.

Fields of the answer: pieces, a list (at most 12, the most important piece first) of objects with
- type: one of bed_double, bed_single, nightstand, wardrobe, dresser, desk, chair, bookshelf
- center: [x, y] of the footprint centre in metres, in the same frame as the room polygon
- rotation_deg: 0..360 counter-clockwise; at 0 the width runs along X and the front faces -Y
- size: [width, depth] in metres, exactly one of the size options of the type
- against_wall: true when the back edge touches a wall
- reason: one short sentence why the piece is there

Answer only with JSON.
